title: Cofactor-normalized fundamental classes of supplied lci curve systems
statement:
Let $p:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes and $F$ a supplied relative-rank-one adjunction system [def-sfb-flat-lci-adjunction-system], indexed by its cartesian base changes [def-sfb-flat-lci-base-change]. For a presentation $C$ on $U$, a comparison $e:C.\mathrm{line}\simeq K$, the actual conormal differential $\delta:A\to V$, and the source differential $\beta:V\to\Omega^1_{U/S}$, a map $\alpha_U:\Omega^1_{U/S}\to K$ has the cofactor normalization if on every open, for every ordered basis $(a_i)$ of $A$ and dual top orientation $\rho$ with $\rho(\bigwedge_i a_i)=1$, and every $v\in V$, one has $\alpha_U(\beta(v))=\epsilon_c e(\rho\otimes(\delta(a_1)\wedge\cdots\wedge\delta(a_c)\wedge v))$. Here exterior powers are [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power], differentials are [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], and $\epsilon_c=1$ for every $c$ in the kernel-first, rank-corrected convention of the supplied system. The scalar Jacobian normalization says that for every additional ordered basis of $V$ there is a trivialization of $K$ taking the image under $e$ of the dual-conormal tensor ambient-volume orientation to $1$, and taking $\alpha_U(\beta(v))$ to $\epsilon_c\det(M)$ whenever the rows of $M$ are the coefficients of $\delta(a_1),\ldots,\delta(a_c),v$ in that basis. In a polynomial chart these are precisely the relations followed by the polynomial being differentiated, so this is the augmented Jacobian determinant, with its orientation fixed by $e$.

A family of maps $\alpha_B:\Omega^1_{X_B/S_B}\to F.L_B$ is a fundamental class in $F$ when (i) on every presentation chart of every base change there is a single local map restricting $\alpha_B$ (equality on universal differential generators, using module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]) which satisfies both normalizations above relative to $F$'s specified local comparison and every actual conormal/source differential map; (ii) its map on the stalk [def-pc-module-stalk-functor] at $x$ is an isomorphism exactly when $p_B$ is smooth on some neighbourhood of $x$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; and (iii) for every cartesian arrow $(g,b):D\to B$, every open $O\subset X_B$ and every $a\in\mathcal O_{X_B}(O)$, the specified comparison $g^*F.L_B\simeq F.L_D$ sends $1\otimes\alpha_B(da)$ to $\alpha_D(d(g^\sharp a))$. This defines a property of supplied data on arbitrary schemes; it asserts no existence and imposes no Noetherian, proper, flat or nodal hypothesis.
